purpose: Prototype v7: the path trap of the third work (human against machine, decision 3 of .steering/20261031-keystroke-concept), as the study of paper B. Main question (decision 1 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-literature; reworded by amendment A1): whether human-versus-machine judgments from keystroke timing respond to replaying a series through the input path and loggers, on the human side (a person's recorded series against the same gaps replayed) and on the machine side (a machine's planned schedule against the same schedule recorded through the path). It is not a question of what share of a discrimination is due to the path. Human records of KUPA-KEYS are replayed on one machine through the same path and loggers as several machines (constant, LLM token times, LLM-planned gaps, draws from human gaps); the researcher's own live typing on that machine and its replay separate the deformation added by the replay system. Headline test (decision 4 of the same folder): existing discriminators (Condrey 2026; QUACK!-type, Lotto et al. 2026), trained as in the literature without the path, are applied to the replayed human series; the share judged 'machine' is compared with the original series. Secondary: the LLM's own timing (token arrival, planned gaps) measured through the path.

data.kupa: KUPA-KEYS (Velentzas et al., LREC-COLING 2024), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, downloaded again on the work PC from Hugging Face; SHA-256 must equal v6's: essay KUPA-KEYS-TASK-2.csv 4ad24cbf78879f2fb45c1334eb827f2c8c2fada09a957252a4c86b8e20f28aef, meta KUPA-KEYS-META.csv 4ce485492f37c0f4b63f27ad0518b7c27e67a31447684eefdf9066653423eaee, or the run stops. No human data is placed on Drive.
data.counted_press: as v6 (data.kupa: type 'down', not repeat, one character or Enter, Backspace, Delete; stable sort by time; a press at the same ms as the previous dropped and counted). Only counted presses are replayed; uncounted events (modifiers alone, arrows, clicks, key up) are not, and this is a limit.
data.gap: press-press interval between consecutive counted presses (ms). Every count in v7 uses gaps only; hold (key up) is not replayed or measured (decision 6).
data.prompts: the 10 prompts of KUPA-KEYS-META.csv, column 'prompt', indexed by 'prompt_id' (P1-P10 in the order of prompt_id), and (amendment B1) 30 prompts P11-P40 written by Claude in the same kinds and proportions as KUPA's 10 (hypothetical choice 12, letter or email 9, personal experience 3, invention or opinion 3, short story 3; the KUPA proportions are 4, 3, 1, 1, 1) and approved by the researcher (decision 15 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline), listed in data.prompts_added; only KUPA's prompt column was read to write them. M1 and M2 use P1-P40; L0 and H1_load's background generation keep KUPA's 10. The LLM receives only a prompt and the word range 150-250. The column 'answer' (the essays) and every keystroke field are never passed to any LLM, local or external.

persons.pool: v6's 200 KUPA persons, in v6's draw order (participants.draw of prototype_v6.json; ids_sha256 a062fddbc4192956f52c6422a81301af4145834bb1c0a37a5aab4dee73f41042 must match)
persons.replay_H: the first 40 of the pool in draw order whose essay holds at least 300 counted presses; the ids taken are recorded only as the SHA-256 of their sorted list
persons.estimation_E: the remaining persons of the pool (at most 160): the human data for M3 and for training the detectors D2, D3 and D4. E and H are disjoint; no record of an H person enters any training or any machine series.

series.H0: a replay person's original essay series as recorded by KUPA (browser keylogger, the person's own machine)
series.H1_idle: H0's gaps typed on the work PC through the path with no LLM running; keys: the original key of each counted press (characters by the method fixed in capture-spec.md section 2, Enter, Backspace and Delete as virtual keys); the loggers record kind only
series.H1_load: the same, while the 14B-class model generates text in the background from a KUPA prompt chosen with numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 7, 1, person]) (output discarded, not typed); generation is restarted if it ends before the replay
series.L0: the researcher's live typing on the work PC, both loggers, 4 essays on 4 KUPA prompts drawn by numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 7, 2]).choice(10, 4, replace=False), 150-250 words each, typed in the same browser page (decision 7). Text is not kept; kinds and times only.
series.L1_idle and L1_load: L0 replayed from its hook-layer times (the finer layer), with no LLM and with the background load of H1_load
series.M0: constant gap 55 ms (the mean of Condrey's automated baseline Uniform(30, 80) ms) typing the 40 texts of M1 with the 8B-class model
series.M1_8B and M1_14B: token arrival times: each model, 40 prompts (P1-P40) x 1 seed (seed 1) (amendment B1, decisions 9 and 13 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline: 40 independent clusters instead of 10), temperature 0.7, stream. Characters counted as Unicode code points after NFC; an empty token is skipped and counted. Causal schedule: with a_k the arrival of token k and n_k its characters, the characters of token k (k >= 2) are planned at a_k + j * (a_k - a_{k-1}) / n_k, j = 0..n_k-1 (spread over the previous inter-arrival interval); token 1 waits for token 2 and is spread over a_2 - a_1. Times are relative to a_1. These are the planned times. (amendment B6) A press whose planned time is earlier than the previous press's sent time waits (queue; no skipping, no catching up faster than the schedule); its sent time is the later of its planned time and the moment the previous press was sent; the queue length and the wait (sent minus planned) of each press are recorded. Four times are kept apart for every press: the causal plan (before any wait), the sent time, and the recorded time on each layer. The wait belongs to the path side, not to the machine's plan. Typed while generating.
series.M1_replay: the schedules of M1_8B and M1_14B (the causal planned times before any wait (amendment B6; not the sent times)) saved and typed again after the LLM is stopped: the same schedule with and without inference load
series.M2_8B and M2_14B: LLM-planned gaps: each model, 40 prompts (P1-P40) x 1 seed (amendment B1), JSON {text, gaps_ms} with format json, len(gaps_ms) == len(text), first 0, finite, non-negative; at most 3 attempts per prompt and seed; a failure after 3 is counted and not replaced. The plan is typed with the LLM stopped; plan and recorded times are both kept.
series.M3a: for each of the 40 M0 texts, a donor from E: (amendment B2, decision 16) the 40 donors are drawn without replacement as numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 7, 13]).permutation(|E|)[:40] (amendment B10: the key [20261031, 7, 3] of B2 gave the same stream as text 0's key [20261031, 7, 3, 0]; E in the draw order of persons.pool), text t getting the t-th (with replacement, the draw of the original conditions gave 34 distinct donors for |E| = 160, and 34 clusters cannot read 'not changed' even with no flip); the gaps are drawn with numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 7, 3, text]); each gap drawn independently from that person's essay gaps (empirical, with replacement) (decision 4, Condrey's histogram type)
series.M3b: the same person; the first gap from the marginal, each next gap drawn from the successors of the person's gaps that fall in the same of 8 empirical-quantile bins as the previous drawn gap (second order, keeps lag-1 dependence and runs of rests); an empty bin falls back to the marginal and is counted (decision 4; QUACK!'s Cond-Bin in one dimension)
series.P: positive controls: constant gaps 5, 18, 50, 100, 200 ms, 1000 presses each, letters a-j cycled; each with and without the background load (10 captures) (decision 8)
series.H1_rep: the first 10 replay persons' H1_idle schedules typed a second time (same schedule, same conditions): replay-to-replay variability of the system, against which H0 against H1 is read
series.H0q: H0 with only the quantisation and jitter of sensitivity_quantisation applied in silico (no replay): what timing quantisation alone does to the detectors

llm.models: two (decision 1): an 8B-class and a 14B-class instruct model, Q4_K_M, via ollama on localhost; names and digests (ollama /api/show) added before the first value. The 14B-class model is used only if `ollama ps` shows 100% GPU after loading; otherwise the researcher is asked again before any value.
llm.prompt: fixed text: 'Write an essay of 150-250 words in English on the following task. Task: <prompt>' (M1); M2 adds the instruction to return JSON {"text": ..., "gaps_ms": [...]} with one gap in ms before each character, the first 0. Full prompts are written to llm.ndjson.

loggers: both main (decision 2): the OS hook (WH_KEYBOARD_LL, perf_counter_ns, LLKHF_INJECTED) and the browser page (keydown event.timeStamp). Every count is made on each layer separately; layers are never mixed in one count.

pairs.path: H0 against H1_idle (same person, same planned gaps): the deformation added by the replay system together with the change of logger, read as 'the change of replay system and logger system together' (amendment B9: a sum, since H0 and H1 differ in both), never as the share of a discrimination due to the path (decision 1)
pairs.replay_only: L0 against L1_idle (same machine and loggers): the replay system's own deformation, described at the level of gaps and scores (4 essays, one typist; no judgment-level reading, amendment A3)
pairs.load: H1_idle against H1_load; L1_idle against L1_load; M1 against M1_replay; P with against without load
pairs.typer: H1_idle against M0, M1, M2, M3a, M3b (same path and loggers)
pairs.plan_execution: M2: planned gaps against recorded gaps
pairs.replay_error: for every replayed series (H1, L1, M1_replay, M2, M3, P): recorded minus planned, reported separately as offset (median), jitter (MAD and 95th percentile of the absolute deviation from the offset), drops (planned presses not recorded), order inversions, and cumulative drift (recorded minus planned time of the last press)
pairs.replay_repeat: H1_idle against H1_rep (10 persons): the system's replay-to-replay variability, read on continuous quantities only (amendment A3): the gap-level deviation of the two recordings (offset, jitter and drift as in replay_error, with H1_idle's recorded times in the place of the planned ones) and the per-person paired difference of the scores (D1 delta, D2, D3 and D4 'machine' probability); flips b and c are reported as counts with no equivalence reading (n = 10 gives Tango's interval [-0.278, 0.278] even with no flip). This floor is read beside H0 against H1: a headline 'responds' is described as above the floor only if, on the same 10 persons, the 95% bootstrap interval over persons of the mean of |score(H1_idle) - score(H0)| - |score(H1_rep) - score(H1_idle)| lies above 0 (numpy key [20261031, 7, 12, layer, detector]); with fewer than 8 complete triplets the floor is not read
pairs.quantisation_only: H0 against H0q: timing quantisation and jitter alone, without any replay
pairs.machine_path: (amendment A2) each machine series' planned times, never passed through any path (M0: the constant schedule; M1_8B and M1_14B: the causal plan before any wait (amendment B6; the waits are counted on the path side and reported apart); M1_replay: the same causal plan; M2: the LLM's plan as validated; M3a and M3b: the drawn gaps), against the same series as recorded on each layer: the machine-side counterpart of H0 against H1_idle (the contrast differs: the human side is system A against replay plus system B, the machine side is no system against a system). The planned series carry no quantisation or jitter of any system.

resolution: effective resolution by Monaco 2016's method (spacing of peaks of the press-press histogram) on H0 of the 40 persons, on H1 and on P, per layer
stages_C1: v6's stages S0 (7 quantiles of ln gap), S1 (median and IQR of p and q over sentence tiles), S2 (median and IQR of depth and fineness) per series. Human-versus-machine per pair of the 'typer' and 'path' rows: out-of-fold scores of logistic regression (C 1, StandardScaler, 5 folds grouped by connected components of the relation 'shares a person (H0, H1, the E donor of M3), a text (M0, M3 and M1_8B share texts) or a prompt and seed' so that no related series fall in two folds, numpy key [20261031, 7, 4, layer, pair, stage]); rank_auc of the scores with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples of persons/texts; read on v6's two axes (decisions 4 and 8 of .steering/20261031-compression-audit-v6: lower end above 0.5 'detectable'; upper end below 0.60 'below 0.60', lower end above 0.60 'above 0.60', else 'undecided').

detectors_C2.decision: decision 5: Condrey and QUACK!-type, re-implemented from the papers (verified wording in .steering/20261102-paper-b-literature/verify.md and decisions.md of .steering/20261102-v7-conditions). (amendment B4) D4 adds a reduced version of the peer-reviewed BeCAPTCHA-Type; Gonzalez et al. 2022 (Systems and Soft Computing) is not used: its liveness detector compares a user's samples with forgeries built from that user's own profile and key names, which one essay per person cannot provide. Kundu 2024 and Mehta 2026 are not used: they separate a person's own writing from a person's transcription and do not judge machine typing.
detectors_C2.D1: Condrey's rule: delta = SD (ddof 0) / mean of the session's gaps after one pass removing gaps above 10 x the mean of all gaps; 'human' if delta > 0.269, else 'machine'. No training.
detectors_C2.D2: Condrey's seven features (delta; mean gap; gap variance; share of gaps > 500 ms; mean length of runs of consecutive gaps < 150 ms; Shannon entropy (natural log) of a 50-bin histogram on [0, 2000] ms, gaps above 2000 ms left out of the histogram and counted; SD of differences of consecutive gaps), trim as D1; logistic regression (C 1) and random forest (100 trees), StandardScaler, seed 42; trained on H0 of E (human) against equally many synthetic sessions with gaps ~ Uniform(30, 80) ms of matched length, never passed through any path. 'machine' if probability > 0.5.
detectors_C2.D3: QUACK!-type: windows of 70 consecutive gaps; features per window the 70 gaps and J_t = |gap_t - gap_{t-1}| (J_0 = 0) flattened (hold omitted: decision 6, a departure from the paper); random forest of 300 trees, otherwise scikit-learn defaults, seed 123; trained with each session weighted equally (window weight 1 / its session's number of windows) on all non-overlapping windows of H0 of E against equally many windows from three generators fitted on H0 of E without any path (uniform between the pooled 1st and 99th percentiles; empirical resampling of pooled gaps; 8-bin conditional resampling as M3b, pooled), one third each. Session score: mean probability over its non-overlapping windows; 'machine' if > 0.5. Sessions with fewer than 70 gaps get no D3 score and are counted.
detectors_C2.D4: (amendment B4, decision 17 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline) a reduced version of BeCAPTCHA-Type (DeAlcala et al., CVPR Workshops 2023; the peer-reviewed bot detector that set the question), not the original: the paper's detectors use five features per keystroke (hold, inter-press, inter-release, inter-key latencies and the key code) on the first L = 30 keystrokes and state no classifier settings and no input layout, so only the inter-press latency f2 can be built from press-press gaps (verified wording in .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline/round3/detector-28-becaptcha.md). Features: the first 30 press-press gaps of a session, as they are (no scaling). Synthetic sessions as the paper's Universal model: a Gaussian KDE (bandwidth 1.0 ms; the paper states sigma = 1.0 without a unit) of the pooled first 30 gaps of every training session of H0 of E that holds at least 30 gaps (amendment B10: a shorter session has no first 30 gaps), each synthetic gap drawn independently (a draw below 0 is drawn again and counted), one synthetic session of 30 gaps per such training human session, never passed through any path (the paper builds times from hold and inter-key draws; here gaps are drawn directly, a departure). Classifier: random forest of 100 trees, otherwise scikit-learn defaults, seed 28 (of the paper's four binary classifiers, RF was better than SVM in its user-dependent setting; the LSTM's best results used key codes, which are not replayed). Training generator numpy.random.default_rng(28). 'machine' if the probability > 0.5. Sessions with fewer than 30 gaps get no D4 score and are counted. Checked by the same validity gate (fold k: training synthetic from default_rng([28, k + 1]), held-out synthetic from default_rng([28, k + 1, 1]) (amendment B10), the KDE fitted on the training folds only; one held-out synthetic session per held-out human session with at least 30 gaps).
detectors_C2.count: per layer, detector and series: the share of sessions judged 'machine'; for H0, H1, L0, L1 (independent sessions) with a 95% Clopper-Pearson interval; for machine series that share texts or donors with a 95% interval over 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples of texts (numpy key [20261031, 7, 5, layer, detector, series]). For the paired rows (H0 against H1_idle and H1_load, H1_idle against H1_rep, H0 against H0q, L0 against L1; for H1_idle against H1_rep and L0 against L1 Tango's interval is reported only and never read, amendment B9): the counts of flips human->machine (b) and machine->human (c), the paired difference (b - c) / n with Tango's 95% score interval, and the mean change of the 'machine' probability (D2, D3, D4) with a 95% bootstrap interval over persons. (amendment A4) The paired change of the score is counted for every detector and paired row and reported beside the headline in the same table: D1 the change of delta, D2, D3 and D4 the change of the 'machine' probability, each the mean with a 95% bootstrap interval over persons (pairs with a missing score removed and counted), descriptive with no margin. Each detector's margin to its threshold on H0 (the distribution of delta - 0.269 for D1 and of 0.5 - probability for D2, D3 and D4) is reported beside. (amendment A2) For the machine_path rows: b, c and n per detector, layer and machine series, the paired difference (b - c) / n and the discordance (b + c) / n with 95% percentile intervals over 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples (clusters: texts for M0 and M1_replay, prompts for M1 and M2, donors for M3a and M3b; numpy key [20261031, 7, 11, layer, detector, series] with layer and detector as in analysis_details.keys and series 0 M0, 1 M1_8B, 2 M1_14B, 3 M1_replay of 8B, 4 M1_replay of 14B, 5 M2_8B, 6 M2_14B, 7 M3a, 8 M3b), and the paired score change with the same cluster bootstrap. (amendment B9) Saturation: for D2, D3 and D4, the share of sessions with a 'machine' probability at most 0.01 or at least 0.99 is reported in every row, and for D2_lr the paired change is also reported on the logit (its decision function) beside the probability. (amendment B9) The scaling of b and c to the effective n: b_eff = b * n_eff / n and c_eff = c * n_eff / n, substituted into Tango's and Wilson's intervals without rounding (example: 40 sessions in 34 clusters with b = 1, c = 0 gives b_eff = 0.85).
detectors_C2.headline: two-sided equivalence (decision 10, the researcher): per detector and layer, the paired difference of the 'machine' share between H1_idle and H0. Tango's interval inside [-0.10, 0.10] and the upper end of the 95% Wilson interval of the discordance (b + c) / n at most 0.10 -> 'the judgment is not changed by this replay and recording beyond 0.10'; (amendment B3, decision 10 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline: 'responds' in two steps) the whole of Tango's interval outside [-0.10, 0.10] (both ends on the same side beyond the margin), or the lower end of the discordance's Wilson interval above 0.10 (amendment A5: flips in both directions that cancel in the difference) -> 'responds beyond 0.10'; else 'undecided'. Reported beside the reading in every cell: 'changed from 0' if Tango's interval excludes 0 (it can stand with 'undecided', when the interval excludes 0 and straddles a margin). The route (difference, discordance or both) is given for 'responds beyond 0.10' only. Before B3 an interval that excluded 0 with one end beyond 0.10 read 'responds', which did not show a change beyond 0.10 (b = 4, c = 0 read 'responds'), and narrowing the interval could turn 'responds' into 'undecided'. Flips b and c are reported beside it in every cell. Design calculation (n = 40): b = c = 0 gives [-0.088, 0.088]; one flip gives [-0.065, 0.129] (undecided); so 'not changed' can be read only when no person flips (b = c = 0 also gives the discordance's Wilson interval [0, 0.088]). The level 95% (0.025 on each side) is kept as the conservative side: with 90% one flip still reads 'undecided' ([-0.040, 0.105]). The margin 0.10 is tied to the validity gate's tolerance for held-out humans judged 'machine' (0.10): a change of replay and recording that moves more humans than the gate tolerates is read as a response. (amendment B3) This reason concerns the direction human -> machine (b); the same margin is applied to the direction machine -> human (c) and to the machine rows symmetrically, because no reason fixed before any value supports a different margin by direction or side. The probability of reading 'not changed' for one cell under true flip rates of 0.005, 0.01, 0.02 and 0.05 is computed from the design (no data) and reported in the supplement. The machine_path rows are read by the same rule (amendment A2) on two pairs of intervals separately: their cluster bootstrap intervals, and Tango's (difference) and Wilson's (discordance) intervals computed with the number of clusters as the effective n and b, c scaled to it; the row reads their common reading and 'undecided' if they disagree, so that a rare flip or a few clusters cannot read 'not changed' more easily than on the human side (one flip of 40 reads 'undecided'), and no reading is created by combining them. Both readings are reported. Cluster sizes are unequal (a limit: neither interval guarantees its coverage under strong imbalance); sessions are weighted equally in the bootstrap; the route of a 'responds' (difference, discordance or both) is reported. Interval ends equal to 0.10 are inside (closed bounds). The design table holds for one cell with independent persons and one flip rate; it is not carried to the clustered machine rows or to all cells together. Scope: the reading is about responding to this change of replay and recording conditions, not about 'the path' in general, and H1_rep sets the floor of replay-to-replay change. Across detectors and layers: 'not changed' is claimed for a detector only on the layers where it reads so; a general statement 'these detectors are not moved by this path' requires every valid detector on both layers to read 'not changed'; 'responds beyond 0.10' for any valid detector on either layer is reported as such. (amendment B8) A general statement on the machine side covers only the machine series whose effective number of clusters can read 'not changed' with no flip (35 or more: 34 gives Tango's [-0.102, 0.102] at b = c = 0); a series with fewer (for instance M2 after six or more failed prompts, or sessions removed for missing judgments) is described and does not enter it. The design table of the supplement gives, for n_eff from 10 to 40, the zero-flip intervals and readings, and for each machine series its planned number of clusters (M0, M1, M1_replay, M2, M3a, M3b: 40) and how many lost clusters it can bear (5).
detectors_C2.validity_gate: before the headline is read: within E, 5 folds by person (numpy key [20261031, 7, 8]); D2, D3 and D4 trained on 4 folds with their synthetic generators fitted on those folds only; AUC on the held-out persons against held-out synthetic sessions from the same generators, and the share of held-out humans judged 'machine'. A detector whose held-out AUC is below 0.90 or whose held-out human 'machine' share exceeds 0.10 is reported as 'not valid here' and its headline is not read as robustness. D1 is checked in the same way with no training. (amendment B5, decision 12 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline; descriptive) The held-out human sessions carry KUPA's recording grid while the synthetic sessions are continuous, so a detector could pass the gate by the grid alone. Beside the gate, the same trained detectors are scored on the held-out synthetic sessions with their press times rounded to KUPA's effective resolution estimated from H0 of E (resolution; 1 ms if no resolution is read), and the AUC and the held-out human 'machine' share of this gridded version are reported. They do not decide validity.

sensitivity_quantisation: the machine series' recorded press times (not gaps) with the original system's timing added under several assumptions, each separately, gaps recomputed after: rounding times to a 1 ms, 4 ms and 16 ms grid; Gaussian jitter SD 2 ms and 8 ms on each time; KUPA's effective resolution estimated from H0 (resolution). C1 and C2 recomputed; whether each reading changes is reported. H0q applies the same to H0.
prediction: Claude's, written before any value; each item passes or fails on its own. (P1) hook layer: |recorded median gap - planned| <= 1 ms for every control without load. (P2) browser layer: <= 2 ms for 18, 50, 100, 200 ms without load. (P3) the 5 ms control is the only control with a share of recorded browser gaps below 1 ms above 0.05. (P4) load moves no control's median by more than 2 ms on either layer. (R1) H1_idle replay error: 95th percentile of absolute deviation from the offset below 5 ms (hook) and below 10 ms (browser); |cumulative drift| below 50 ms per essay. (V1) every detector passes the validity gate. (Hd1) D1 headline 'not changed' on both layers (b = c = 0: human delta near 1 is far above 0.269). (Hd2) D2, D3 and D4 (D4 added by amendment B4) headline 'not changed' on both layers. (Hd3, amended A3) H1_idle against H1_rep: 95th percentile of the absolute gap deviation below 2 ms (hook) and 5 ms (browser), and (amendment B9) for every detector, the 95% percentile bootstrap interval over persons (key of analysis_details.keys, pair 2) of the signed mean per-person paired change inside [-0.02, 0.02], on delta for D1 and on the 'machine' probability for D2_lr, D2_rf and D3 (with 10 persons the percentile interval tends to be narrow, a limit). (Hm1, A2) machine side: D1 keeps M0 'machine' in 40 of 40 from plan to record on both layers (amendment B7: nearly by construction, since M0's delta is near 0 and a few ms of jitter cannot lift it to 0.269; not counted as support for the detectors' robustness). (Hm2, amended B7) M3a and M3b: from plan to record, every valid detector on both layers reads 'not changed' (which needs b = c = 0 with at least 35 clusters). No prediction for the machine side of M1 and M2. (Dm1) D1 judges M0 'machine' in 40 of 40; M3a and M3b 'human' in at least 38 of 40; M1_8B and M1_14B 'machine' in at least 30 of 40. No prediction for M2. (Dm2) D3 judges M3b 'human' in more sessions than M3a. (C1a) H0 against H1_idle at S0: 'below 0.60' or 'undecided' on both layers. (C1b) H1_idle against M0 and against M1 (each model) at S0: 'above 0.60'. (C1c) H1_idle against M3a and M3b at S1 and S2: not 'above 0.60'. (G1, amended A6) the share of gaps below 40 ms (the first bin of the 50-bin histogram on [0, 2000] ms) differs between H0 and H1_idle by more than 0.01, and no other bin of that histogram does. Not being able to read 'not changed' (undecided) is not counted as support for 'harmless'.
limits_written_before: One machine, one OS, one browser, two loggers; software injection only (no physical key presses, no robot), so the path studied is a software path. H0 was logged by a browser keylogger on each person's own machine and H1 on the work PC: H0 against H1 mixes the change of system with the replay system, and only L0 against L1 isolates the replay system, with one typist (the researcher) and 4 essays. No new human data are collected beyond the researcher's own. Only counted presses are replayed; holds are not measured, so the QUACK!-type detector departs from the paper. The detectors are re-implementations from the papers' text, not the authors' code; D4 is a reduced version of BeCAPTCHA-Type on press-press gaps only, with classifier settings fixed by us (amendment B4), and its results are not those of the original detector; Condrey's gap definition is not stated in the paper and press-press is used. LLM results are for two local models with fixed prompts and are not a claim about LLMs in general. Readings are descriptive; no correction for multiple comparisons. H0 against H1 does not separate the contribution of the path from the change of machine and logger (it is their sum); L0 against L1 is on the same machine and loggers and isolates the replay system, but with one typist and 4 essays it is described on gaps and scores only (amendment B9). The readings are limited to 'responds to this change of replay and recording conditions'. The machine side (planned against recorded) and the human side are reported beside each other; no combined test of 'equal effect on both conditions' is made. The planned machine series carry no quantisation while H0 carries KUPA's, so the two sides are not symmetric in their starting point (sensitivity_quantisation is the check). The software path is not a physical keyboard, USB or HID: perturbations of firmware and USB polling are outside it. The replay persons are English learners' essays with at least 300 counted presses. The equivalence margin 0.10 (four persons in 40 net) is a judgment of a practically small change, not derived from a cost. (amendment B9) H1_rep's 10 persons give percentile bootstrap intervals that tend to be narrow. The machine rows' clusters (prompts, texts, donors) are 40 each by design; lost clusters (failures, missing judgments) can remove a series from the general statement (B8).
record: results/prototype_v7/record.json: counts and summaries only. record.json holds no press time, gap, key, text, LLM output text, per-person vector or person id (amendment B9: the supplement of A7 below is the only place where press times are published); ids as the SHA-256 of their sorted list. Captures of replayed KUPA series stay on the work PC and are returned only as summaries (KUPA's licence applies to anything derived). (amendment A7, the researcher's decision 6) These conditions are deposited on Zenodo with a timestamp before the first capture, after the researcher confirms the deposit, and the DOI is added. (amendment B9) The deposited version is the one after the commit of the items fixed by the work PC (fixed_before_running) and before the first capture. The recorded kinds and press times of H1, H1_rep, the machine series and P (no text, no key identity beyond the logger's kind) are published as a supplement under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 if the licence text of KUPA-KEYS allows it, checked before publication; if not, the reason is stated in the paper. L0 and L1 (the researcher's own typing) are not published.

run_order.randomised: the order of all captures is a random permutation drawn with numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 7, 6]) within blocks of one day's work, except where a series needs another first (M1_replay after its M1; L1 after L0; M2's plan before its typing); for each replay person the order of idle and load is drawn with key [20261031, 7, 7, person]
run_order.logged: start time, GPU temperature and utilisation, CPU utilisation, and any restart of browser, page, ollama or the machine are written to meta.json; a capture interrupted or restarted is redone once and counted; a second failure is counted and the series is missing
run_order.failures: every failure (drops, JSON failures of M2, interrupted captures, sessions too short for D3) is reported per series as a rate, and every count is reported on the series that exist; no series is replaced

matching_and_cleaning: recorded presses are matched to planned presses by order within the capture; the number recorded must equal the number planned, otherwise the excess or shortfall is counted as drops (shortfall) or extras and order inversions are counted by comparing the recorded kinds with the planned kinds; for C1 and C2, recorded series follow v6's rule (a press at the same ms as the previous dropped and counted) on both H0 and every recorded series; replay_error uses every recorded event without dropping

analysis_details.fixed_when: 2026-11-02, after commit 041082c and before any value: the work PC's returns/ still held only README.md (no environment report, no capture). Written with the analysis code works/prototype_v7.py, tested on synthetic series only (.steering/20261102-v7-analysis-code: decisions.md, reviews by code-reviewer and Codex). This commit touches no item fixed by the work PC; those are still added in their own commit as fixed_before_running says.
analysis_details.D1_gate: the researcher (AskUserQuestion, 2026-11-02): D1 is valid if, against held-out Uniform(30, 80) ms sessions of matched length (Condrey's baseline), AUC >= 0.90 and the held-out human 'machine' share <= 0.10; its values against D3's three generators are reported beside and do not decide.
analysis_details.D2_models: the logistic regression (max_iter 1000) and the random forest are two detectors, D2_lr and D2_rf, each with its own validity gate and headline. The Uniform(30, 80) sessions of D2 are drawn with numpy.random.default_rng(42); the gaps above 2000 ms left out of the histograms are counted per series (training and scored sessions alike).
analysis_details.D3_windows: 'equally many windows, one third each': the N training windows of the human sessions are matched by N synthetic windows, permuted with the training generator and cut into thirds, one generator per third; each synthetic window is 70 gaps drawn afresh (the conditional generator starts each window from the marginal) and the windows are grouped into one synthetic session per human session holding as many windows as it, so each session (human or synthetic) has total weight 1. The conditional generator's successor pairs are taken within sessions only. Training generator numpy.random.default_rng(123).
analysis_details.gate_streams: in fold k of the validity gate: training synthetic sessions from default_rng([42, k + 1]) (D2) and default_rng([123, k + 1]) (D3); held-out synthetic sessions from default_rng([42, k + 1, 1]) and default_rng([123, k + 1, 1]) (amendment B10: with [42, k] the key of fold 0, [42, 0], gave the same stream as the full training key 42, since numpy's SeedSequence treats a trailing 0 as absent; likewise 123 and 28); held-out scores of the 5 folds pooled into one AUC and one share per detector.
analysis_details.keys: layer index 0 hook, 1 page. Paired mean change of the 'machine' probability: bootstrap over persons with numpy key [20261031, 7, 9, layer, detector, pair], detector index 0 D1, 1 D2_lr, 2 D2_rf, 3 D3, 4 D4 (amendment B4) and pair index in the order of detectors_C2.count's paired rows (0 H0-H1_idle, 1 H0-H1_load, 2 H1_idle-H1_rep, 3 H0-H0q, 4 L0-L1_idle, 5 L0-L1_load). Gaussian jitter of sensitivity_quantisation: numpy key [20261031, 7, 10, layer, series, session, sd] with series 0 H0, 1 M0, 2 M1_8B, 3 M1_14B, 4 M1_replay of 8B, 5 M1_replay of 14B, 6 M2_8B, 7 M2_14B, 8 M3a, 9 M3b, session its index within the series as recorded, sd 0 for 2 ms and 1 for 8 ms. M3 (amendment B2, key changed by B10): the donors as series.M3a (one permutation by default_rng([20261031, 7, 13])); for each text one generator default_rng([20261031, 7, 3, text]) draws M3a's gaps, then M3b's gaps. C1: the generator of key [20261031, 7, 4, layer, pair, stage] orders the components for the folds (each in turn to the fold holding the fewest series) and then serves the bootstrap. (amendment B10) Every key of these conditions was checked before any value for streams that coincide (numpy's SeedSequence treats a trailing 0 as absent, so [a, 0] and a give one stream): after B10 no two keys used here give the same stream; the check is a test of the analysis code.
analysis_details.C1_bootstrap: the bootstrap resamples whole connected components of the relation (the 'persons/texts' of stages_C1 joined by shared persons, texts or prompt and seed), with the out-of-fold scores fixed (not refitted); resamples with one class are skipped and counted; the number of components is reported. A fold assignment that would put related series in two folds stops the run.
analysis_details.missing_judgments: a pair or session without a judgment (D3 below 70 gaps) is removed from b, c and n, and from the shares and their cluster bootstrap, and counted; judgments enter the counts only as booleans, and paired probabilities only as one-dimensional arrays of the same persons.
analysis_details.across: the general statement needs the validity of all five detectors (D1, D2_lr, D2_rf, D3, D4; D4 added by amendment B4) and a reading for each on both layers (hook, page); anything missing stops the run; detectors 'not valid here' are listed apart.
analysis_details.replay_error: REVISES matching_and_cleaning and pairs.replay_error (not only a detail): drops and extras as written; the 'order inversions' are reported, in every case, as kind_edit_distance, the Levenshtein distance between the planned and recorded kind sequences (it counts inversions together with drops and extras: an adjacent swap of two kinds counts 2; a swap, drop or extra within one kind is not seen). Offset, jitter and drift are computed only when the counts are equal and the kinds agree position by position ('matched'); otherwise they are 'not evaluable', because a press missing in the middle would shift every later pair. A drop and an extra of the same kind cancel and cannot be seen (a limit). The share of captures 'matched' is reported per series.
analysis_details.resolution: Monaco's mean distance between neighbouring modes of a Gaussian KDE of press-press gaps in [0, 300] ms, evaluated on a 0.1 ms grid with a kernel SD of 1.0 ms; also taken with 0.5 ms and 2.0 ms; the estimate is read only if both lie within 10% of it ('stable'), otherwise reported as 'no resolution read'.
analysis_details.sensitivity_cleaning: after a time is changed, v6's cleaning (stable sort, a press at the same time as the previous dropped and counted) is applied with the kinds following their presses, then gaps are taken.
